questions.q: Underneath Salesforce's UI, what does a relationship field like Opportunity.AccountId actually store?
options: The ID of the related record on the other object -- the same idea as a SQL foreign key
A full copy of the related record's data
A text description of the relationship
Nothing -- relationship fields are purely a UI display feature with no underlying data
questions.explain: A relationship field is a field on one object storing another record's ID, exactly like a foreign key.

questions.q: What makes a Salesforce relationship field more than a plain foreign key, per this lesson?
options: The relationship TYPE you choose changes real behavior -- delete behavior, security inheritance, and whether roll-up summaries are possible
Salesforce relationship fields cannot store an ID at all
Relationship fields only work between two custom objects, never a standard object
There is no real difference -- it behaves exactly like a plain foreign key in every way
questions.explain: The relationship type (Lookup vs. Master-Detail) carries non-negotiable rules about delete, security, and rollups.

questions.q: How does Salesforce natively represent a many-to-many relationship, like Contacts to Campaigns?
options: It doesn't have a native many-to-many field type -- you build a junction object with two Master-Detail relationships
With a single field that stores a list of many IDs at once
Many-to-many relationships are impossible to build in Salesforce
By duplicating the Contact record once per Campaign it relates to
questions.explain: Salesforce has no native many-to-many field; the junction object pattern (two Master-Detail relationships) implements it.

questions.q: Per this lesson, which relationship shape is loose and optional -- a child record can exist without its parent?
options: Lookup relationship
Master-Detail relationship
Junction object relationship
All relationship types in Salesforce are equally loose
questions.explain: Lookup relationships are loose and optional; Master-Detail is the tight, required relationship, covered next lesson.

questions.q: Why does this lesson introduce object relationships before the next course teaches SOQL?
options: Because SOQL joins across objects use exactly these relationship fields, and the syntax won't make sense without the underlying mental model first
Because SOQL doesn't actually support joins of any kind
Because relationships are unrelated to SOQL and this is just general background
Because Salesforce plans to remove relationship fields in a future release
questions.explain: SOQL child-to-parent and parent-to-child queries walk relationship fields directly -- this chapter builds that foundation first.
